Mary Peltola

Registered Democrat candidate for United States Senator, Alaska · Challenger

Former U.S. Representative; former tribal judge

Mary Peltola is a Yup'ik Alaskan and former tribal judge. She represented Alaska's at-large U.S. House district from 2022 to 2025 and was the first Alaska Native member of Congress. She lost re-election to the House in 2024 and is now the Democratic nominee running against incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Peltola stands

Iran / foreign policy
Argues that the war with Iran has raised fuel and living costs in Alaska, saying Alaskans are "being priced out" because of the war. Criticizes Sullivan's support for the war.
Energy and cost of living
Says that if elected she would work to speed up federal reviews of resource development projects under laws such as the Endangered Species Act and NEPA.
Fisheries
Calls for more NOAA funding and blames federal budget cuts for problems in the fishing industry. Argues that federal fisheries policy should focus on wild-caught fish rather than farmed fish.
Fisheries science and federal workforce
Opposes cuts to NOAA and to the federal fisheries science workforce that came through the Elon Musk-led cost-cutting initiative.
